title: The Oldest Customer Complaint on Record (c. 1750 BC)
description:
3,700 years ago, a man in Ur paid for fine copper, got bad copper, and wrote the angriest letter he could. It's the oldest customer complaint on record.

Sources:
- British Museum, museum no. 1953,0411.71 (BM 131236): clay tablet, letter from Nanni to Ea-nasir about the wrong grade of copper, from Ur, Old Babylonian period, c. 1750 BC (date approximate). Excavated by Sir Leonard Woolley.
- Guinness World Records, 'Oldest written customer complaint'.
- Cultural Property News, 'The Internet's Favorite Sumerian'.
Sound and visuals are original; narration is a synthetic voice.
